articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This 'EPHEMERIS' for March 2013 details the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities for March and April, including star parties, dark-sky weekends, solar observation sessions, and beginner astronomy classes. It also announces an advanced topics meeting, an auction, and a general meeting featuring Dr. Nathalie Cabrol on astrobiology. Additionally, the document provides information on two bright comets, ISON and PanSTARRS, predicted to be visible in 2013, offering guidance for observers.

articles.title: Comets
articles.summary: The article explores the unpredictable allure of comets, featuring prominent examples like Hale-Bopp and Hyakutake that spurred amateur astronomy, alongside anecdotes of amateur discoveries and a personal observation of Comet Holmes. It also briefly covers recent comet-focused space missions before shifting to Jupiter observing, detailing the "Whac-a-moon" phenomenon—brief appearances of Galilean moons due to eclipses—and offering specific viewing times for these celestial events.

articles.title: Directions to Houge Park
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to Houge Park, located in San Jose near Campbell and Los Gatos. It includes turn-by-turn instructions from both Hwy. 17 and Hwy. 85, guiding visitors to the park's entrance and parking lot.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures
articles.summary: The free Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures have restarted at Foothill College after a year-long sabbatical due to renovations, though parking costs $3. Upcoming talks include Gibor Basri on Brown Dwarfs and Free-floating Planets on April 17, and Lori Fenton discussing the Surface of Mars on May 15. Past lectures are available online.

articles.title: NASA Space Place
articles.summary: This article explains how NASA develops ideas for new astronomy and astrophysics missions, primarily through the Decadal Survey conducted by the National Research Council. The 2010 survey, "New Worlds, New Horizons," outlined high-priority research objectives for the next decade, focusing on early universe formation, exoplanets, and fundamental physics. The top recommended large mission for 2012-2021 is the Wide-field Infrared Survey Telescope (WFIRST), aimed at studying exoplanets and dark energy, though its timeline is subject to budget constraints.

articles.title: Auction XXIII
articles.summary: The article announces the annual SJAA Auction XXIII, scheduled for March 24th at Houge Park. Additionally, it features several astronomy news updates from early 2013, including the Curiosity rover's first successful drill operation on Mars, research on the potential for nearby Earth-like exoplanets orbiting red dwarfs, a description of the open cluster NGC 411, and the projected collision of Betelgeuse with a bar of interstellar material.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: This article from the SJAA Ephemeris provides updates on the San Jose Astronomical Association's activities, announcing upcoming Board of Directors elections for February and detailing a revamped telescope loaner program, including the new QuickSTARt initiative. It also presents a comprehensive report on school star parties, showing completed events from July to January and scheduled events for the 2012/2013 school year, alongside contact information for officers, staff, and various SJAA programs.
